statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-33634 is a supply-chain compromise of upstream Trivy release artifacts, including the malicious v0.69.4 release binary and v0.69.5/v0.69.6 Docker Hub images, injected at build or publish time via stolen Aqua credentials in March 2026. The malicious code was not committed to the Trivy source tree. The Trivy Operator image builds v0.31.1 from source and embeds github.com/aquasecurity/trivy v0.71.0 as a Go module dependency, which was published after the incident from clean source; the compromised release artifact code is not present in the runtime binary.

The Trivy Operator image builds v0.31.1 from source and embeds github.com/aquasecurity/trivy v0.71.0 as a Go module dependency, which was published after the incident from clean source; the compromised release artifact code is not present in the runtime binary.

CVE-2026-33634 is a supply-chain compromise of trivy release binaries v0.69.4 through v0.69.6, injected at build time via stolen Aqua credentials in March 2026. The malicious code was never committed to the trivy source tree. Zot v2.1.17 depended on github.com/aquasecurity/trivy v0.70.0, and Zot v2.1.18 depends on v0.71.1; both versions were released after Aqua rebuilt from clean source, so the compromised release artifact code is not present.

CVE-2026-33634 is a supply chain compromise that affected only the upstream aquasecurity/trivy v0.69.4 release published on 2026-03-19. The CVE description explicitly identifies versions 0.69.2 and 0.69.3 of the Trivy binary as known-safe. The DHI alpine variant ships trivy 0.70.0 or later (currently 0.71.2-r1), which was tagged and built from the rebuilt upstream source after the incident with rotated credentials and is not the malicious v0.69.4 artifact. The DHI debian variants build trivy 0.71.2 from source with COMMIT_SHA verification (commit 055a5c8a53bfd61f7a8e276a5b2f0c3fc1673420) and never pull the upstream prebuilt binary; this scanner false positive does not affect them. The advisory range >=0.69.4 with no fixed version is overly broad relative to the actual incident scope. Every DHI trivy build is produced from clean upstream source (the git tag for debian, the rebuilt apk for alpine) and never the compromised registry artifacts, at any version, so the trivy product is matched version-lessly here to keep this statement valid across version bumps; the earlier per-version PURLs are retained for older builds.
